## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)
- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Keep the original graph and all vertices. Handle n = 0 directly with optimum value 0 and the empty set for both problems. An isolated vertex must belong to every independent dominating set.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n)$ |
| Clauses | $O(n+m)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. For a threshold b, impose independence by $\neg x_u\vee\neg x_v$ for every edge uv and require $\sum_v x_v\le b$. For each vertex v use an optional marker y_v with $\neg y_v\vee\neg x_u$ for all u∈N[v]. Compute marker parity by full-equivalence XOR gates.

2. Take the exact count with even marker parity minus that with odd parity. For each independent set S obeying the threshold and any fixed x-bits, its contribution is $\sum_{T\subseteq U(S)}(-1)^{|T|}$. This is 1 exactly when S dominates G. The difference therefore counts independent dominating sets within the budget and is positive exactly when such a set exists. Here U(S) is the set of vertices undominated by S.

3. Each test uses two formulas with 2n selection/marker variables, at most n−1 parity outputs, and O(n) counter/comparator auxiliaries. There are O(n+m) clauses of width at most three. Gate extensions are unique for fixed x and y. The explicit CNF bit length is O((n+m) log(n+2)); the two counts and their difference use O(n) bits, so construction and exact arithmetic are polynomial in L.

4. Binary search on b∈[0,n] takes O(log(n+1)) feasibility tests, each using two exact #SAT calls. At the optimum b*, fix each original x_v to 0 if the parity difference with that additional unit clause is positive, and to 1 otherwise. At most n further tests recover an independent dominating set of size exactly b*. Retain all prior choices and the original graph throughout.

5. An independent dominating set is exactly an inclusion-maximal independent set. Its complement is an inclusion-minimal vertex cover. Thus if the minimum independent dominating size is i(G), the largest inclusion-minimal vertex cover has size n−i(G), and complementing the recovered set produces an optimum Upper Vertex Cover solution.

6. The polynomial number of sequential exact-counting calls gives A(n)L^{O(1)} time and polynomial space; the reported formalization assumption gives its separate weaker bound. For m≤Dn with D fixed, N+M=O_D(n), so forced-zero padding and the sparse assumption also give B(n)L^{O(1)}.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- Upper Vertex Cover maximizes the size of an inclusion-minimal cover. It is different from Minimum Vertex Cover, whose complement is a maximum independent set.
- The feasibility oracle uses the sign of an exact even-minus-odd count. The satisfiability of either auxiliary formula alone does not establish independent domination.
- This entry uses original vertex count n, not a solution-size parameter. No weighted extension, enumeration bound, novelty claim, or latest-best comparison is included.

The derivation must preserve the objective and account for the encoding length of numerical values; a decision consequence alone does not establish the stated optimization bound.
